subject: Conditional annualization + overage smoothing proposal for renewal
messages:
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acme-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal question — smoothing overages during first year

Hi Hannah,

We're starting our renewal discussions and looking at a 36‑month commitment, but we'd like to propose a slightly different structure for the first 12 months. Our usage has spiked unpredictably this quarter as we onboard two new product lines. We'd like to avoid a big true‑up at year end.

High level ask: can Redwood offer a conditional annualization for year 1 where we lock in a lower committed baseline (co‑term with current calendar) but have an "overage smoothing" band — up to 25% over baseline would be billed at a reduced overage rate, and anything above that triggers a mid‑year review and option to purchase burst capacity at a discounted uplift. We also want a clear path to co‑term the following two years.

Related context: our procurement prefers annual invoices but can accept quarterly true‑ups if the smoothing band is in place. We can share usage files for Jan–May to help size the baseline.

Can your team put together a proposal that includes pricing math, legal language for the conditional clause, and a pragmatic rollforward for year 2?

Thanks,
Sarah

Sarah Lewis
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Analytics
Phone: +1 (415) 555‑0123

Attachments: acme-usage-jan-may-2027.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 12:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal question — smoothing overages during first year

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the usage file. We can absolutely structure something like this; I sketched an initial option below and will follow up with a short spreadsheet and proposed contract language.

Proposal (summary):
- Term: 36 months, co‑term starting 2027‑07‑01 (aligns with your fiscal Q3).
- Year 1 baseline: 600k tokens/month (proposed based on early read of your Jan–May file).
- Overage smoothing band: up to 25% above baseline billed at baseline_rate * 1.15 (15% uplift) rather than standard overage.
- Burst/Surge: usage beyond 125% billed at baseline_rate * 1.6; a mid‑year review clause triggers at sustained usage >140% for a 30‑day window and includes option to purchase additional committed capacity at a pre‑agreed uplift (discount vs list).
- Conditional annualization (rollforward): at the 12‑month anniversary, the baseline will annualize to max(actual_avg, baseline) subject to a 20% cap increase unless Acme elects to pin earlier.
- Auto‑renew: standard auto‑renew for years 2–3 unless Acme provides 90 days notice; however, we can add a one‑time auto‑renew exception for Year 2 to allow you to renegotiate if average usage remains >130% for months 10–12.

I'll loop in Finance (Monica) and Legal (Karthik) to validate pricing and contract language. Expect a formal spreadsheet and a redline snippet by EOD tomorrow.

Hannah
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (650) 555‑9821

Attachment: redwood-conditional-annualization-v1.xlsx (proposal spreadsheet, 18KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal — Acme renewal: conditional annualization + smoothing band (need approvals)

Team — quick internal thread to confirm we can offer the commercial mechanics below. External is already looped and expects a formal response. Key asks: pricing math sanity check, confirmation we can include a one‑time auto‑renew exception, and whether Legal is comfortable with the mid‑year review trigger language.

Recap of customer and ask:
- Account: Acme Analytics (ACME‑2027‑RNW‑578)
- They want a 36‑month commitment but need Year 1 to have flexibility to avoid a large true‑up.

Proposed mechanics (from my draft):
1) Year 1 baseline = 600k tokens/month (we used Jan–May to propose).
2) Overage smoothing: usage between 100%–125% charged at baseline_rate * 1.15.
3) Surge billing: usage >125% charged at baseline_rate * 1.6.
4) Mid‑year review: sustained >140% over a 30‑day rolling window triggers a commercial review and option to purchase burst capacity at baseline_rate * 1.45 (pre‑negotiated uplift).
5) Annualization at month 12: baseline becomes max(actual_avg, baseline) but capped to +20% unless Acme opts for a higher baseline.
6) One‑time auto‑renew exception: At year 2 renewal, if months 10–12 average >130% then Acme may reopen pricing/commit for that renewal window (requires 60‑day notice).

Questions for Finance (Monica & Markus):
- Is 15% reduced overage uplift reasonable vs our standard 25%? Impact on ARR and expected unit economics?
- For surge pricing (1.6x), can we commit to the burst purchase option at 1.45x? How does that affect margin with committed discounts?

Question for Legal (Karthik):
- Can you draft a short clause for the mid‑year review (trigger threshold & remediation path)? We should avoid ambiguous terms like "sustained" — suggest "30‑day rolling average >140% of baseline". Also confirm language to limit customer right to repeatedly reopen Year 2 (one‑time only).

I suggest we tell the customer we'll deliver the redline and the final spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow, pending approvals.

Thanks — Hannah

---
On Wed, 26 May 2027 at 11:03 AM, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hannah / team – quick finance note: 15% uplift on smoothing seems acceptable for enterprise accounts in this bracket; our modeling shows a ~6.8% ARR downside versus full baseline annualization but materially reduces churn risk.
>
> Surge/burst pricing at 1.6x is fine, but the pre‑negotiated burst purchase at 1.45x will need to be limited to one purchase window per 12 months to protect margin. Recommend adding that cap to the clause.
>
> I'll update the spreadsheet with the ARR delta and a simple P&L view.
>
> Monica
> Finance — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal question — smoothing overages during first year

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the usage file and the good convo. Below is the formalized option we've agreed internally; attaching the pricing spreadsheet and a short contract snippet for review.

Formal proposal (high level):
- Term: 36 months, co‑term date 2027‑07‑01.
- Year 1 baseline: 600k tokens/month (based on Jan–May data).
- Overage smoothing band (100–125%): billed at baseline_rate * 1.15.
- Surge band (>125%): billed at baseline_rate * 1.6. A one‑time burst purchase at 1.45x is available if sustained usage exceeds 140% over a rolling 30‑day window; this option is limited to one purchase per 12‑month period.
- Annualization: at month 12 baseline will be set to max(actual_avg, baseline) but increase will be capped at +20% unless Acme elects to increase earlier.
- Auto‑renew clause: standard auto‑renew applies years 2–3; we will add a one‑time year‑2 reopen right if months 10–12 average >130% (customer must provide notice 60 days prior to renewal).

What we attached:
1) redwood-conditional-annualization-v1.xlsx — pricing math and simple ARR/P&L impact.
2) contract_snippet_conditional_annualization.docx — suggested legal language for the smoothing band, mid‑year review trigger, burst purchase limit, and year‑2 reopen right.

Next steps:
- Please review and tell us if the smoothing uplift (15%) and the burst mechanics are acceptable by Tue, 1 Jun.
- If yes, I'll put together a final amendment and route for signatures (DocuSign).

If you'd like, we can also schedule a 30‑min call to walk through the spreadsheet with Monica to show the ARR modeling.

Best,
Hannah
